column1: # IceCubes landing series — the tracked, machine-readable record of what landed.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The close gate's first policy stage decides whether a batch may land by
# reading `.claude/claims.md`: ~990 KB of prose, 2160 lines, 214 MERGE-DONE entries, ZERO git
# history — and `Scripts/gate.sh` deliberately walks OUT of the gated worktree to read the steward
# checkout's single mutable copy (`${git_common_dir:h}/.claude/claims.md`). A fresh clone could
# therefore not reproduce a single merge verdict, and an audit citation into that file
# (claims.md:2418) was already past EOF within hours of being written.
# THE PROSE LEDGER STAYS UNTRACKED, DELIBERATELY. `.gitignore` calls it the "Multi-agent claims
# lock — out-of-band, never merged": several lanes append to it concurrently and tracking it would
# make every lane conflict on every landing. So what is committed here is not the prose — it is the
# SERIES the stall detector actually consumes, one line per landing, nothing else.
# APPEND-ONLY, AND ORDERING IS NOT SIGNIFICANT. `.gitattributes` gives this file `merge=union`, so
# two lanes that land in parallel each keep their line without a conflict — and the union driver may
# interleave them in ANY order. `Scripts/validate-icecubes-close-policy.rb` therefore sorts by the
# recorded UTC stamp (ties broken by sha, which is total and clone-independent) and never by file
# position. Never rewrite, reorder, or delete a line: a landing that happened is a fact about
# history, and the validator refuses a candidate whose series drops or rewrites a line its merge
# base already carried.
# FORMAT — one landing per line, five TAB-separated fields, no trailing tab:
#   <sha40>\t<utcStamp>\t<scoredScreens>\t<owedR2AE>\t<rungs>
# `#` lines and blank lines are ignored. Any OTHER line is a hard parse error, because a field this
# file cannot read is a verdict nobody can reproduce, which is the defect being fixed.
# EVERY FIELD IS DERIVED FROM GIT AT THAT SHA, NEVER TYPED. Append with
#   /usr/bin/ruby Scripts/validate-icecubes-close-policy.rb --record <gated-sha>
# which derives all five fields itself and is a no-op when the sha is already present. Run it AFTER
# the gate, next to the `MERGE-DONE` post: appending before the gate would change the tree and
# therefore change the very sha the line describes. Each close re-derives and COMPARES every field
# it depends on, so a hand-typed number reds the gate instead of becoming history.
# The command behind each field, all reproducible from a fresh clone:
#   sha40          git rev-parse <sha>^{commit}
#   utcStamp       git show -s --format=%ct <sha>, formatted %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ in UTC
#                  (the epoch is used rather than a `--date=` spelling so the value does not
#                  depend on the TZ of whichever machine recorded it)
#   scoredScreens  the number of R2_FLOORS entries in `git show <sha>:Scripts/icecubes-r2.sh`
#   owedR2AE       their sum, EXCLUDING screens that board marked `# ACKNOWLEDGED <screen>:` at
#                  that sha — the same figure the stall detector has measured since 2026-08-03
#                  (LOOP-ICECUBES.md §13), so a screen at 0 cannot mask a screen at 50,184
#   rungs          git show <sha>:Sources/IceCubesCheck/IceCubesCheck.swift \
#                    | grep -ohE '"R[0-9][a-z-]*"' | sort -u | wc -l
#                  (the same selection `Scripts/validate-anti-drift.sh` ratchets, so the function
#                  half of the north star is recorded per landing rather than only at HEAD)
# A LINE'S VALIDITY IS ESTABLISHED BY ANCESTRY, NOT BY THE PROSE RECOGNISER. `--record` refuses to
# append a sha that is not an ancestor of the integration base, because the fields alone cannot tell
# a landing from an abandoned lane tip or a rebased predecessor — `git rev-parse` resolves all three:
#   git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main
# That matters most for the backfill below, whose SELECTION came from the ledger's `MERGE-DONE`
# prose. That recogniser matches the marker as a substring, and this repository has already recorded
# a MERGE-LOCK/PROGRESS note that merely MENTIONED a landing being read as an entry for it. A line
# that came out of prose is therefore only trustworthy because ancestry was checked afterwards —
# never because a sentence contained the word.
# BACKFILL. The first ten lines were reconstructed on 2026-08-08 from the ten distinct MERGE-DONE
# shas the ledger then carried — the detector window is five landings, so this is two windows of
# depth. Nothing here was invented: every field was produced by the commands above, run against the
# tree at that sha. Every one of the ten was then re-checked against the ancestry rule above and
# all ten passed (origin/main at 1d7db92c, 2026-08-08); none was dropped or corrected:
#   for s in $(grep -v '^#' Docs/icecubes-landing-series.tsv | cut -f1); do \
#     git merge-base --is-ancestor $s origin/main && echo "OK $s" || echo "FAIL $s"; done
